reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality of communicative systems lies in the tension between rigidity and learning. Rigidity, modeled as a constraint on information flow, corresponds to low entropy states where minimal change occurs. Learning, conversely, is characterized by increasing entropy due to new information integration. These patterns form a dualistic framework where entropy acts as a dynamic variable that governs adaptation. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian updating under entropy constraints. In GSE, it translates into state transitions governed by entropy thresholds. Failure modes emerge when rigidity dominates (no learning), or when entropy exceeds channel capacity (information loss). The mathematical structure is defined by a feedback loop where entropy drives learning, which in turn modifies rigidity parameters.
